package_info.why_malicious: This report is a general discussion of software supply chain risks and the importance of vetting open-source packages. It does not describe a specific malicious package or code, but highlights that many supply chain attacks involve nefarious or faulty open-source code, which can introduce vulnerabilities or malicious behavior into software ecosystems.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests during package installation or import
Access to sensitive files or environment variables by third-party packages
Execution of code at install-time or import-time without clear justification
file_indicators: Presence of scripts in setup.py, package.json, or .github/workflows that perform network or file operations
Unusual or obfuscated code in open-source dependencies
network_indicators: Outbound connections to unknown or suspicious domains during build or install processes
Exfiltration of data to external endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for open-source packages that execute code during installation or import, especially those that access sensitive files or environment variables, or make outbound network requests. Use automated curation tools to block or flag packages with known vulnerabilities, suspicious behaviors, or unvetted origins before they enter the software supply chain. Maintain an audit trail of all third-party components and their behaviors.
